The majority voted in favour of disagreeing with the [amendment](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debate/?id=2020-04-08.18.1) to the usual second reading motion "*that the bill be read [for a second time](https://peo.gov.au/understand-our-parliament/how-parliament-works/bills-and-laws/making-a-law-in-the-australian-parliament/)*", which is parliamentary jargon for agreeing with the main idea of the bill. This mean that the amendment failed. This amendment was introduced by Gorton MP [Brendan O'Connor](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/representatives/gorton/brendan_o'connor) (Labor) and, if it had been successful, its text would have been added to the usual second reading motion as a note. In other words, it didn't seek to change the actual text of the bills. MP O'Connor explained [the rationale behind his amendment](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debate/?id=2020-04-08.18.1) in his contribution to the debate. ### Amendment text > *That the following words be added after paragraph (6):* > > *"(7) calls on the Government to ensure that the JobKeeper wage subsidy is only used by employers to pay their employees’ wages and not to subsidise their company’s balance sheet, noting that there should be no provision for business to force employees to use their annual leave entitlements and pay for that leave with the JobKeeper wage subsidy".*

speeches.speaker: Christian Porter
speeches.brief: A motion was moved to suspend standing orders to rearrange the day's sitting, prioritising debate on the Coronavirus Economic Response Package (Payments and Benefits) Bill 2020, the Coronavirus Economic Response Package Omnibus (Measures No. 2) Bill 2020, and Appropriation Bills Nos 5 and 6 of 2019-2020. The motion, agreed with the Manager of Opposition Business, sets debate until 2 pm, cancels the Federation Chamber, and prescribes grouped voting on amendments.

speeches.speaker: Katrina Allen
speeches.brief: The Coronavirus Economic Response Package (Payments and Benefits) Bill would support six million workers and provide a $130 billion economic bridge, with public health measures including 30 million PPE sets, ICU capacity doubled from 2,200 to 7,500, and 2.5 million telehealth visits.

speeches.speaker: Richard Marles
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Coronavirus Economic Response Package bills and moved an amendment to extend JobKeeper payments to working visa holders unable to return to their country of origin. They also called for including casuals employed less than 12 months and for parliamentary scrutiny through a Senate select committee chaired by Senator Katy Gallagher.

speeches.speaker: Nicolle Flint
speeches.brief: The speaker argued in support of the $130 billion JobKeeper package, announced that eligible businesses would receive $1,500 per fortnight per employee, and thanked workers, businesses, and the public for their sacrifices during the pandemic.

speeches.speaker: Zali Steggall
speeches.brief: The speech argued that the government's COVID-19 economic response packages, while welcome, have gaps that exclude casual employees, pay-as-you-go contractors, temporary visa holders, and self-funded retirees, and urged extensions of support to these groups, as well as greater oversight for commercial tenancies and childcare.

speeches.speaker: Helen Haines
speeches.brief: The independent MP supported the JobKeeper payment as a major improvement but noted it fails to cover casuals employed for less than 12 months, affecting 20% of workers in her electorate. She welcomed free childcare but warned the rushed package threatens rural providers' viability, and called for guarantees that all providers be eligible for JobKeeper and no provider be worse off, while arguing for joint parliamentary committees to scrutinise the government's pandemic response.

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: The opposition moved an amendment to the Coronavirus Economic Response Package Bill 2020, requiring the Treasurer to consider support for casuals, prevent employers from using wage subsidies to cover leave entitlements, and address gaps for charities, universities, NDIS providers, temporary visa holders, and local government employees. The amendment also sought to prevent employers from coercing workers into taking leave in exchange for JobKeeper eligibility.

speeches.speaker: Michael Sukkar
speeches.brief: The government rejected amendments to the Coronavirus Economic Response Package, arguing the JobKeeper scheme already provides a wage guarantee for six million Australians, supports businesses to survive the crisis, and extends to part-time and long-term casuals using established industrial relations definitions, while charities and not-for-profits are also covered with donations factored into the turnover test.

speeches.speaker: Adam Bandt
speeches.brief: The Greens MP supported opposition amendments to include casual workers and others left out of the government’s package, and asked the minister whether JobKeeper eligibility could be extended to workers with a proven income history but not employed on 1 March (e.g., arts workers on short-term contracts). The MP also asked the minister to confirm that the bill’s rules cannot be used to take away existing entitlements under other acts or schemes.
